title: Copilot Studio: persistent identity (agent accounts) for agents
summary: The briefing largely matches Microsoft's Frontier preview documentation, including its licensing and shared-memory risks. Hold because the agent-blocking path omits the required confirmation action after selecting Block; the comparison with how agents previously ran also lacks supporting documentation.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Makers can give a Copilot Studio agent its own identity in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: An account gives a Copilot Studio agent its own identity in Microsoft 365 so it can take a business process from start to finish on its own. With an account, your agent has its own Microsoft Entra ID, mailbox, and presence across Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Without this feature an agent was something that only ran behind a maker or a shared service connection.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agents accounts previously maker shared service connection identity. Read authoring-agent-account, admin-use-entra-agent-identities and govern-agents-identities-overview. None states this exclusive historical authentication model.
claims.fix: Remove 'rather than something that only runs behind a maker or a shared service connection' from the first paragraph of What's changing.

claims.claim: After publishing, an agent's own mailbox can send and receive email and be added to distribution lists.
claims.quote:
After you publish it, your agent works as a member of your organization:
- It has its own mailbox, so it can send and receive email and be added to distribution lists.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A published agent appears in Teams and the organisation's directory, subject to the stated EEA Teams qualification.
claims.quote: It appears in Microsoft Teams and your organization's directory, where people can find and @mention it like a colleague.

claims.claim: Colleagues can find and @mention the agent.
claims.quote: It appears in Microsoft Teams and your organization's directory, where people can find and @mention it like a colleague.

claims.claim: Supported operations can use the agent's own scoped access rights.
claims.quote: Supported operations can use the agent's own scoped access rights.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Tools configured for end-user authentication use the agent's identity and consent.
claims.quote: Tools configured for end-user authentication use the agent's identity and consent.

claims.claim: The agent does not respond to anyone outside its tenant in this preview.
claims.quote: External users: the agent doesn't respond to anyone outside its tenant. There's no workaround in this preview.

claims.claim: The agent responds only in email conversations with up to 250 people.
claims.quote: Email audience: the agent responds only in email conversations with up to 250 people.

claims.claim: The agent cannot co-author changes to existing documents.
claims.quote: Document editing: generating new documents is supported; editing existing documents through co-authoring isn't supported yet.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Protected documents; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Agents with accounts cannot read documents protected with labels such as Confidential or Internal Only.
claims.quote: Agents with an account can't read protected documents. For example, they can't access documents protected with Confidential or Internal Only sensitivity labels, or the equivalent for your organization.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationales: risk and impact
claims.claim: The agent keeps one shared memory across everyone it works with, learning from conversations for later responses.
claims.quote: Memory lets an agent retain what it learns in conversations, such as preferences, context, and how work gets done, and apply it in later conversations. In an agent with its own account, that memory is shared.

claims.claim: Shared memory has no privacy boundary between users.
claims.quote: The agent is guided not to bring up one person's details with someone else, but shared memory has no privacy boundary between users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Shared memory; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The People card warns that shared files and chats can appear in responses to people without access, regardless of sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: The agent's People card displays this notice: "Any files or chats you share can be summarized and included in the agent's responses to any user, even users without permissions to the files or chats and regardless of sensitivity label."

claims.claim: Shared memories are deleted after 28 days without anyone interacting with the agent.
claims.quote: If no one interacts with the agent for 28 days, the system automatically deletes its shared memories.

claims.claim: End users cannot opt out of shared memory in this preview.
claims.quote: No. End users can't opt out of shared memory in this preview. By using the agent, you consent to its use of shared memory.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].note; controls[3].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An admin must turn off agent accounts altogether to turn off shared memory in the preview.
claims.quote: In this preview, shared memory can't be turned off independently of agent accounts. To turn off shared memory, an admin must turn off agent accounts altogether.

claims.claim: Each agent with an account has its Microsoft Entra account and a separate Microsoft Entra Agent ID.
claims.quote:
The agent has its own Microsoft Entra account and identity, so admins can govern and audit it like any other identity.
Copilot Studio also creates a Microsoft Entra Agent ID that admins manage separately, for each agent that has an account.

claims.claim: An agent account does not automatically grant every tool permission.
claims.quote: The agent account does not automatically grant every tool permission. Check which identity a tool uses and grant only the access needed for the job.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The agent's email address cannot be changed after publishing.
claims.quote: You also can't change the email address for your agent after you publish the agent. Plan your agent's identity before publishing.

claims.claim: The maker-based alias prefix cannot be changed during the preview.
claims.quote:
The agent's email address uses your own alias as a fixed prefix, and the agent reports to you.
During this preview, you can't change the maker-based alias prefix or reporting relationship.

claims.claim: The agent's reporting relationship cannot be changed during the preview.
claims.quote: During this preview, you can't change the maker-based alias prefix or reporting relationship.

claims.claim: Agents with accounts can run through configured triggers.
claims.quote: Configure supported tools and a recurrence trigger; instructions alone don't create a schedule or grant access.

claims.claim: Agents with accounts can generate new documents.
claims.quote: Document editing: generating new documents is supported; editing existing documents through co-authoring isn't supported yet.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio data policies can restrict connector tools and supported agent capabilities, rather than providing a universal per-account action allow-list.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.claim: Tenant-scoped data policies apply to all agents in all environments across the tenant.
claims.quote: Policies with a tenant scope apply to all agents in all environments across the tenant.

claims.claim: The feature page does not publish the Frontier for AI Teammates licence price.

claims.quote: Searched: full authoring-agent-account licensing and prerequisites, and microsoft-agent-365/frontier licensing FAQ. The feature page describes Frontier account licensing; the FAQ's GA rule names Agent 365 and E7, not the Frontier for AI Teammates account licence.
